notes: §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR3: WRITE ... FROM is 'MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1 according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement' and then the same WRITE without FROM. KeyedIoBinder#BindWrite binds the implicit MOVE through MoveBinder#BindFromPhrase (so the MOVE legality rules apply: a noninteger FROM to an elementary alphanumeric record is refused, COBOL0819, §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3 c), and KeyedIoEmitter#EmitWrite emits that MOVE before the I-O; VersionConformancePass#VisitRecordFromPhrase refuses FROM literal, ZERO and ALL literal at 85 (COBOL0871). Probes at 85: FROM a group, a reference-modified item, a signed item into a group record, an 18-digit integer (left-justified, truncated), FUNCTION UPPER-CASE, an ODO group into a RECORD VARYING file (length 4 read back) all give MOVE results; a WRITE failing 22 leaves the moved data in the record area; FROM a numeric function is refused (COBOL1914). Not this rule: WRITE RR FROM RR is accepted (SR1, kb/Work PB5077).

next.reason: 2023 adds FROM literal-1 (§2023:14.9.51.4 GR5: "MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1"), which the 1985 format refuses; the FROM identifier-1 case is unchanged. 1985: WRITE FROM = 'MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1' per MOVE rules, then the WRITE without FROM. §2023:14.9.51.4 GR5 keeps the same equivalence ('MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1'); §2023:14.9.51.3 SR6 requires the MOVE to be valid. FROM literal-1 is a different operand the 1985 format lacks; an overlapping identifier-1 (refused by 1985 SR1) still gets MOVE-then-WRITE, as GR3 states. Same.
